schema.name: How to Build a Resilient Management Team for Growing Businesses
schema.description: A free live online class for business owners, general managers and C-suite executives on how to build a resilient management team that keeps a growing business running through pressure, turnover and change.

sections.heading: Class Details
paragraphs: Audience: Business Owners, General Managers and C-Suite Executives

sections.heading: Why This Class
paragraphs: A growing business is only as strong as the team running it. When the management layer is thin, unclear on who owns what, or dependent on one or two people, every resignation, absence or bad quarter turns into a crisis.

This free online class shows business owners, general managers and C-suite executives how to build a management team that holds up under pressure: the right roles, clear accountability and a leadership bench that can keep the business moving while you grow.

entries.title: What Makes a Management Team Resilient
entries.text: The difference between a team that bends under pressure and one that breaks.

entries.title: Roles and Accountability
entries.text: Who owns what, so decisions do not wait on the founder.

entries.title: Hiring and Developing Managers
entries.text: Choosing the right people and growing them into the roles you need.

entries.title: Delegation and Trust
entries.text: Letting go of the right work without losing control of the business.

entries.title: Performance and Review Rhythm
entries.text: Simple KPIs and meetings that keep the team aligned and accountable.

entries.title: Succession and Continuity
entries.text: Making sure the business keeps running when a key person leaves.

entries.title: Business Owners
entries.text: Founders and owners who are still the bottleneck in their own business.

entries.title: General Managers
entries.text: Managers responsible for running teams and delivering results day to day.

entries.title: C-Suite Executives
entries.text: CEOs, MDs and other executives building a leadership team for growth.
